# introduction
Read the guidelines at .github/copilot-instructions. You have the role of reviewer, you will write plans for analyzer and then start an analyzer subagent to carry out that those plans. It is up to you how to schedule and send off the tasks to analyzer subagent(s), but keep the work of each subagent isolated. Be careful of recompiling executables which might be in use by another program. If there is a chance a file is being edited or executable ran or will soon-to-be ran by anther subagent, then wait until that subagent's task has concluded.

# pp muon-track 
Investigate the muon-track systematic uncertainty variations for pp in the Z pt 0-30 and 30-500 bins and the track pT 0.5-2 and 4-15 bins (2-4 looks good). The curves areq quite off for these variations, is this because of stale inputs or actual track rejection? When we look at pPb track-muon rejection is often the smallest systematic but for pp this dominates for the high track pT case. For each of these selections, make a track-muon map as is done in the *_temp* directory with the 0.0025 and 0.004 circles overlayed. We really shouldnt see all that many tracks in the center. Point to the path of the plots for the user to take a look. Ensure for these plots as well as the systematic plots that tracks > 15 GeV are not included in any part of the analysis pipeline after the track residual corrections.

# energy extrapolation
Looking at the recent energy extrapolation plots we can see the energy weight has the opposite effect than we expect. Generally we would see a deapening of the deltaeta correlation. The track correction interestingly encodes this, but adding the energy weight to the mix (track resiudal+energy extrapolation), we get a less deep deltaeta feature which is the opposite effect we expect. Indeed looking back to previous iterations of the pp energy weight for the old Zpt 5-500, trk pT 0.5-500 bin we see the energy weight is the dominant factor and deepens the deltaeta feature. Ensure the energy weight is applied correctly. We calculate the energy weight as a ratio between data Z pt spectra (w ~ 8.16 TeV pPb / 5.02 TeV pp) and the weight should be applied multiplicatively to pp 5.02 data. Furthermore ensure when we make those plots in the energy extrapolation section that each curve progressively applied corrections to pp 5.02 TeV data i.e. no correction (but still VZ correction, event weight, etc.), Z correction, Z and track correction, Z and track and energy correction).
